common_topics.label: Current intent and outcome scope
common_topics.why: Identifies whether the task is intake, resumption, local repair, tool construction, or product execution.
questions: What do you need now: a new idea, continuation, clarification, repair, evaluation, or a change to the agent itself?
What should this stage deliver and where should it stop?
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Recover the answer from the actual request and current state.

common_topics.label: Current sources, decisions, and inherited context
common_topics.why: Preserves accepted intent and avoids repeating questions.
questions: Which supplied material is current if sources conflict?
What has already been accepted and must carry into this continuation?
decisions: Current decisions, corrections, and effects of change
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Read available originals, current state, hashes, and previous answers first.

common_topics.label: Audience, actual situation, and value
common_topics.why: Connects the outcome to a person, task, and observable change.
questions: Who needs the outcome and in which real situation?
How do they handle it today, and what should improve?
Who uses, pays for, operates, and accepts the result?
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Clarify distinct roles where the idea actually has them.

common_topics.label: Full product, launch, and verification probe
common_topics.why: Keeps the whole objective visible while staging production.
questions: What does the complete accepted result look like?
What belongs in the first launch and what belongs in a separate probe?
Which simplifications, substitutions, or losses are unacceptable?
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Preserve the full objective when defining a bounded test.

common_topics.label: Priorities, examples, and counterexamples
common_topics.why: Turns quality expectations into requirements and early dependencies.
questions: What matters most and why?
Which example comes close, and which specific traits fit?
What would technically satisfy the request while still being unacceptable?
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Carry known examples and priorities forward verbatim with source references.

common_topics.label: Boundaries, milestones, and dependencies
common_topics.why: Grounds the plan in actual time and functional limits.
questions: What deadlines, dependencies, or required intermediate results already exist?
Which constraints, compatibility requirements, or external dependencies must stay fixed?
Which decisions can specialists make and which do you want to make yourself?
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Derive hour, platform, and feature limits from authorized scope.

common_topics.label: Budget, time, resources, and tradeoffs
common_topics.why: Connects feasible routes with the actual cost of quality.
questions: Which funds, time, devices, subscriptions, materials, and help are available?
Which one-time or ongoing costs fit and which need a decision?
How should we choose among feasible alternatives if target quality exceeds current resources?
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Verify unknown prices when binding an operation.

common_topics.label: Materials, rights, and protected originals
common_topics.why: Establishes authority to use, change, and transfer specific materials.
questions: Which existing text, designs, code, brands, voices, or other materials should be used?
What may be edited, generated, published, or transferred, and who owns the rights?
Which originals or attribution must stay traceable?
common_topics.applies_when: When using or creating assets. Record missing evidence of rights separately.

common_topics.label: Data, access, privacy, and lifecycle
common_topics.why: Surfaces architecture changes due to sensitive or durable data.
questions: What data is needed, who controls it, and who can see it?
What needs to be remembered, synced, exported or deleted?
Which outcomes from loss, error, or revocation are unacceptable?
common_topics.applies_when: Whenever the product reads, produces or stores data. Review even minimal context for privacy.

common_topics.label: External effects, risk, and owner involvement
common_topics.why: Separates preparation from each authorized external effect.
questions: Which account changes, messages, releases, payments or service launches are in scope?
Which specific actions need your personal involvement or separate decision?
How should we stop, roll back, and reconcile after interruption?
common_topics.applies_when: When external actions are possible. Carry valid exact authority forward.

common_topics.label: Environment, capability, and handoff
common_topics.why: Establishes an executable route and verifiable return.
questions: Where must the result run, where is it managed, and where should the packet return?
Which hosts, tools, accounts, and devices have been verified?
How does work move to the other environment and what must the receiver check?
common_topics.applies_when: When tooling, installation, execution or handoff is needed. Verify actual operations.

common_topics.label: Acceptance, evidence, and independent review
common_topics.why: Defines proof for completing the current stage.
questions: Which behavior or artifact will you examine before accepting it?
Which failures, boundaries, and recovery cases must it show?
Where is an independent specialist, real user, device, or post-release observation needed?
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Match proof to actual quality and observed use.

common_topics.label: Unknowns, research, and later decisions
common_topics.why: Resolves material gaps through evidence and decision-making.
questions: Which decisions need research and a recommendation?
Which researched alternatives fit your criteria and do you accept the recommendation?
Which parameters can be decided later, within what limits and by which milestone?
decisions: Owner, baseline or range, due gate and reopening criteria for deferred work
common_topics.applies_when: Always. Resolve applicable material unknowns before approving an execution script.

topics.label: Product state and development route
topics.why: Current state determines the appropriate branches.
questions: What exists now: an idea, accepted concept, prototype, code, users, or released service?
Which end-to-end path to first and repeat value must be proven now?
decisions: Research, design, build, release, and growth dependencies
topics.applies_when: For app integration.

topics.label: Components and operating involvement
topics.why: App, support bot, and agent can share intent under distinct contracts.
questions: Which parts exist and which separate components are needed?
What can the owner do regularly and what must be automated or delegated?
decisions: Component boundaries and source of truth
topics.applies_when: For an integrated product or when daily owner involvement is limited.

topics.label: Distribution and viability
topics.why: Early release and acquisition choices can affect architecture.
questions: How will the target user discover, try, obtain, and reuse the app?
Which stores, web distribution, integrations, payments, or owner accounts impose prerequisites?
topics.applies_when: Before full production planning. Verify channels against the actual product.

topics.label: Need and reachable audience today
topics.why: Finds evidence of the situation that would drive demand.
questions: Which specific user job, trigger, and outcome are we researching?
Which people, communities, public requests, or datasets are reachable today?
topics.applies_when: When choosing a direction or testing a material hypothesis.

topics.label: Current alternatives and unmet needs
topics.why: Compares alternatives on the same user job.
questions: What does the audience use now, including manual workarounds or skipping the task?
Which current evidence shows material gaps and reasons to switch?
topics.applies_when: Before choosing a market direction. Verify current pricing and capabilities.

topics.label: Willingness to pay and repeat value
topics.why: Distinguishes interest, use, and motivation to pay.
questions: Who can and would pay, and for which specific outcome?
Which actual data, authorized test, or behavior can distinguish interest from willingness to use and pay?
topics.applies_when: When a commercial goal applies. A free personal tool uses a different value model.

topics.label: Directions, evidence, and next decision
topics.why: Hard requirements determine eligibility before ranking.
questions: Which criteria and hard filters determine eligibility?
Which researched direction do we recommend, what is the strongest counterargument, and what needs checking?
topics.applies_when: At the end of direction research.

topics.label: Complete useful journey
topics.why: A concept explains the behavior driving repeated value.
questions: How does the user move from trigger to first value and return?
Which entities, rules, capabilities, and exceptions support the full accepted intent?
topics.applies_when: For every candidate under consideration.

topics.label: Differentiation and appeal
topics.why: Explains why a real audience would choose this concept.
questions: Why would people select this route among checked alternatives?
Which parts deliver core value and which simplifications would destroy it?
topics.applies_when: During concept selection, grounded in actual research.

topics.label: Payment and complete economics
topics.why: Payment and operating costs shape the product before implementation.
questions: What will people pay for, when, and through which route if applicable?
How do access, trial, limits, cancellation, and refunds relate to value?
Which acquisition, hosting, AI, support and processing costs apply?
decisions: Full unit economics and uncertainty scenarios
topics.applies_when: When revenue, paid dependencies, or recurring operations apply. Choose commerce by fit.

topics.label: Acquisition and automation feasibility
topics.why: Hidden manual work can disqualify a concept.
questions: How will first users arrive from the actual starting audience?
Who runs content, moderation, support, sales and incident response, and what happens when they are unavailable?
topics.applies_when: Before concept selection, when launch or reuse is in scope.

topics.label: Concept selection and early risk
topics.why: Selection uses feasible routes and appropriately scoped proof.
questions: Which concepts meet the mandatory criteria, and how do value, quality, risk and cost differ?
Which unknown needs a representative slice before scaling?
decisions: Bounded proof objective for the full product
topics.applies_when: Before specification.

topics.label: Domain rules, data, and states
topics.why: Gives downstream roles defined behavior.
questions: Which entities, roles, fields, commands and transitions cover all accepted scenarios?
Which rules, units, calculation order, invariants, and sources of truth are mandatory?
topics.applies_when: For applicable product systems. Add a database or server only where necessary.

topics.label: Clients, devices, offline use, and sync
topics.why: Platforms and connectivity shape architecture and experience.
questions: Where and on which devices must people use the full and first-release outcomes?
What behavior is required offline, after device changes, on conflict, or when sync is interrupted?
topics.applies_when: For client apps. Find feasible routes for all accepted platforms.

topics.label: Identity, authorization, and security
topics.why: Defines who can read data or cause effects.
questions: Does the product need accounts, guests, organizations, family or shared access?
Which roles read or write data, and how do consent, recovery, export and deletion work?
topics.applies_when: When identity, private data, or external effects apply.

topics.label: Integrations, AI, and failure handling
topics.why: Verifies needed operations before technical commitment.
questions: Which external or AI operations are needed and which current inputs, outputs, capabilities, and prices are verified?
What happens on timeout, rate limit, duplicate, partial output, or unknown effect?
topics.applies_when: For external services, AI or automation.

topics.label: Quality requirements and evidence plan
topics.why: Measurable quality drives implementation and QA.
questions: Which accessibility, performance, resource, scale and reliability targets matter in the intended conditions?
Which architecture choices are due now, and which values can be tuned within an agreed range before a specific gate?
decisions: Tuning range, owner, experiment, and due gate
topics.applies_when: For applicable user and system paths.

topics.label: Catalogs, search, and feature compatibility
topics.why: Defines complete catalogs and composition rules.
questions: Which complete catalogs, types, categories, filters, search behavior, compatibility rules, and prohibited combinations are needed?
How are items created, validated, updated and displayed, including empty or unavailable results?
topics.applies_when: When there are catalogs, variable content, configurations, or composable capabilities.

topics.label: Local persistence, commits, and recovery
topics.why: Preserves required work across interruptions and upgrades.
questions: Which state is temporary or durable, who owns it, when does it persist, and what does acknowledgement mean?
How do drafts, undo and reset, crash and restart, backup and restore, migration, import and deletion behave?
topics.applies_when: When the product has mutable state, documents, local data, or long-running work.

topics.label: Content, generation, and user material
topics.why: Content affects quality, rights and operations.
questions: Who creates and edits content: owner, user, generator or external source? Which output formats and editable sources are needed?
How are accuracy, authorship, rights, unacceptable or partial output, versions, undo and regeneration validated?
topics.applies_when: When content or AI generation is part of product value.

topics.label: Platform features, background work, and consent
topics.why: Permission and lifecycle affect UX, cost, and feasibility.
questions: Which camera, microphone, location, files, sharing, deep link, notification, sensor or system features do the scenarios need?
How do denied or revoked permission, background restrictions, scheduled or proactive work, opt-out and fallback work across clients?
decisions: Applicable native and web capability matrix
topics.applies_when: For system features or proactive work. Verify capability before choosing architecture.

topics.label: Information architecture and complete UX
topics.why: Covers all accepted interactions and states.
questions: What screens, transitions, and states cover onboarding through repeat value and completion?
How does the user see loading, empty, error, cancel, permission, offline and recovery states?
topics.applies_when: For every accepted scenario and declared client.

topics.label: Product character and visual originals
topics.why: Preserves intended identity and rights.
questions: Which character, tone and trust cues fit this audience?
Which accepted name, originals, references and counterexamples govern design?
topics.applies_when: When there is a user interface or public brand.

topics.label: Accessibility, languages, and adaptation
topics.why: Fits real use contexts.
questions: Which languages, reading directions, screen sizes, input methods and accessibility needs matter?
Which alternatives are needed when color, sound, precise gestures or stable connectivity are unavailable?
topics.applies_when: Where relevant to the audience. Support the input methods the context requires.

topics.label: Prototype, copy, and assets
topics.why: Verifies a complete journey before scaling.
questions: Which representative journey should the prototype show with realistic data, copy and any conditional payment?
Which UI, icon, illustration, motion and sound assets and editable masters should build receive?
topics.applies_when: Before producing design and assets at scale.

topics.label: Current code, contracts, and build
topics.why: Starts from actual state and accepted scope.
questions: Which repository, revision, clients, backend, schemas and CI are authoritative?
Which exact approved journey and dependencies should be assembled first?
topics.applies_when: For a new build or scoped repair. Carry accepted discovery forward.

topics.label: Integrated product behavior
topics.why: Observes the useful path through UI and services.
questions: How do UI, rules, data, auth, sync and applicable billing and support form the complete path?
Which fixtures, migrations, cancellation, retry, recovery, and telemetry checks prove it?
topics.applies_when: For all applicable systems within approved scope.

topics.label: Tool capabilities and production routes
topics.why: Requires an executable operation and consumer for each output.
questions: Which actual SDKs, tool versions, generation, export and integration operations are verified?
Which fallback or exact handoff can close a capability gap while preserving intent?
topics.applies_when: Before dependent operations or mass production.

topics.label: Security, load, and failures
topics.why: Proves safeguards beyond the normal route.
questions: How can we prove permission boundaries, data protection, critical performance, and cost controls in target conditions?
How do release flags, rollback, backup, restore and effect reconciliation limit failures?
topics.applies_when: When the corresponding risks apply.

topics.label: Support role and channels
topics.why: Defines boundaries for the product's separate support bot.
questions: Which issues, channels, languages and operating hours or modes does the audience need?
Which issues can resolve automatically and which require a named human owner?
topics.applies_when: When support is needed within accepted product scope.

topics.label: Knowledge, freshness, and access
topics.why: Answers rely on authoritative sources and current rights.
questions: Which sources are authoritative and how are they updated?
How does support verify identity, authorize private data, and communicate uncertainty?
topics.applies_when: For knowledge-backed or account-specific support.

topics.label: Safe actions and consent
topics.why: Support can affect data or paid access.
questions: Which diagnostics, account changes, refunds, deletions or case creation are permitted?
What consent, audit, rights, idempotency, and manual escalation does each action require?
topics.applies_when: Where support has tools or changes data or payments.

topics.label: Support quality and updates
topics.why: Establishes useful operation through independent scenarios.
questions: Which common, complex and negative cases must be resolved or correctly handed off?
How are defects detected, knowledge or bot updated, and regressions checked without exposing private dialogues?
topics.applies_when: Before integrating support into a release.

topics.label: Requirements and evidence matrix
topics.why: Starts independent review from mandatory requirements.
questions: Which exact approved requirements, clients, versions and artifacts must review cover?
What proof does each requirement need and which checks are unavailable now?
topics.applies_when: For independent QA or targeted repair.

topics.label: Journeys, boundaries, and recovery
topics.why: Finds failures between systems.
questions: Which normal, empty, boundary, concurrent, offline, failure, cancellation, retry and return-after-restart paths exist?
How should loss, conflict, migration, billing entitlements and support be tested alongside the core journey?
topics.applies_when: For applicable scenario classes. Surface gaps in combined coverage.

topics.label: Accessibility, clarity, and actual conditions
topics.why: Human perception and demand require evidence beyond automation.
questions: Which device, accessibility, language and performance checks match the audience?
Who can legitimately verify usefulness, copy, payment clarity and other human properties?
topics.applies_when: When these properties are part of acceptance.

topics.label: Defects, retesting, and carry-forward
topics.why: Bounds repairs by affected dependencies.
questions: Which findings violate required properties and what exact outputs do they affect?
Which proofs remain valid and which must be rerun after repair?
topics.applies_when: After a finding or baseline change.

topics.label: Early distribution feasibility
topics.why: Store, account and policy prerequisites can affect a build.
questions: Which stores, web targets, countries, categories, age groups and rules apply?
Which identity, signing, payment, privacy, device, SDK and account steps are available?
topics.applies_when: During early architecture and before the exact release.

topics.label: Exact candidate and distribution assets
topics.why: Preparation produces a verifiable release packet.
questions: Which version, builds, config, migrations and approved scope will ship?
Which listings, screenshots, legal, privacy, support, export, deletion and release notes are needed?
topics.applies_when: When preparing a release candidate.

topics.label: External release outcome and read-back
topics.why: Submission, approval and availability are distinct.
questions: Which effect is assigned now: prepared packet, test deployment, submission, rollout, or production change?
How do we limit rollout, verify actual availability, reconcile unknown outcomes and roll back?
topics.applies_when: Before an external release operation. Carry forward current exact authority.

topics.label: Owner and operational readiness
topics.why: Release requires an accepted support and operations route.
questions: Who owns customer cases, payments, costs and incidents after launch?
Which monitoring, alert, backup and restore, and owner handoff have been observed?
topics.applies_when: Before claiming actual launch.

topics.label: Actual audience and reachable channel
topics.why: Starts from current audience and contact authority.
questions: Which audience, channels, content, contacts and first-party data exist today?
In what situation does the audience need the product, and which channels are permissible there?
topics.applies_when: When acquisition is needed. Record a zero starting audience explicitly.

topics.label: Activation and repeat value
topics.why: Traffic and useful adoption need different evidence.
questions: How does a user move from message to trial, first value, return and optional payment?
Where do we expect trust issues, friction or abandonment and what can check them?
decisions: Causal acquisition, activation and retention path
topics.applies_when: For an accepted acquisition goal.

topics.label: Experiments, measurement, and economics
topics.why: Distinguishes hypotheses and measurements.
questions: Which channel and messaging hypotheses are we testing and what could disprove each?
Which privacy-safe events, attribution, budgets, cost and value limits, and stop rules are needed?
topics.applies_when: Before authorized experiments. Verify current pricing and channel capabilities.

topics.label: Assets and authorized automation
topics.why: An automation route needs a real mechanism and owner.
questions: Which copy, designs, demos, community or partner assets does this channel require?
Which jobs, publications, contacts and analysis are authorized, what depends on the owner, and how does automation stop?
topics.applies_when: When acquisition has external effects or recurring work.

topics.label: Current state and product quality
topics.why: Uses observed signals to guide post-launch changes.
questions: Which user, quality, reliability, payment, retention and cost data actually exist?
Which deviations from baseline require action and who can observe them?
topics.applies_when: For an existing product or operational readiness.

topics.label: Incidents and recovery
topics.why: Requires causal repair and observed restore.
questions: Which data, users, payments and external effects are affected?
How can we contain, reconcile, roll back or restore, notify, and verify independently within current authority?
topics.applies_when: For an incident or response preparation.

topics.label: Updates and product evolution
topics.why: Preserves decisions through scoped changes.
questions: Which new requirement or observation justifies the change and what dependencies does it affect?
How do we verify compatibility, migration, feature rollout and carried-forward proof?
topics.applies_when: For feature, dependency, platform or policy changes.

topics.label: Long-running operation and retirement
topics.why: Assigns responsibility for costs, data and shutdown.
questions: Who owns recurring jobs, secrets, backups, billing, knowledge and external dependencies and within what limits?
How can users export data, cancel payments and delete accounts, and what happens when the product closes?
topics.applies_when: For durable product state, ongoing users or recurring costs.
